goal: Land, in ONE PR and in this order, two coupled changes to the cmux dispatcher. (A) Fix a LIVE outcome-classification bug: a gate/adapter-composed BLOCKED markdown return is currently recorded as outcome: 'ok' (a clean success). classify() sets bodyStatus: null for every markdown body (ladder.mjs:423 — a markdown body is a string, it has no status field), so OUTCOME_MAPPING's completed -> ok row (dispatch.mjs:109) fires for it. This has been live since #6 pane-dispatched six markdown roles. Fix: classify() derives a new bodyBlockedMarkdown flag from the EXACT first line writeBlockedReturn composes, and a new OUTCOME_MAPPING row keyed on that flag sits ahead of the completed -> ok row. (B) Flip pane: true for code-reviewer, code-reviewer-deep and build-validator, which requires the roster + PANE_ROLES + their agent definitions + the coherence tests to move as ONE atomic commit, and requires each of those three agent files to author the Verdict/Must-fix/Notes sections its roster entry already demands. A must be committed and green BEFORE B: B is what makes the (A) bug reachable for three more roles, and A's tests are the proof the classifier no longer launders a gate kill into a success. Two commits, one PR, A first.
constraints: conventions.md: every functional commit bumps .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version and the commit message ends '; bump 0.<major>.<minor>'. Two functional commits (A, then B) = two bumps.

conventions.md 'prefer structural impossibility to a test assertion, and a whitelist to a blacklist': the blocked-markdown first-line literal is defined ONCE in contract.mjs (BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX) and imported by both the composer (return-lint.mjs) and the recognizer (ladder.mjs); no second copy of the string 'status: blocked - ' may exist in scripts/cmux/*.

conventions.md: a worker's self-reported terminal status is decided at the outcome-mapping layer, never inferred from the process exit sentinel. New OUTCOME_MAPPING row goes ahead of 'completed' and must not read fsState.exitSentinel.
backend-notes.md: cross-test-file constant agreement is guarded by source-text extraction (readFileSync + regex), never by importing another test file.

architecture-notes.md 2026-08-03 'Roster required_sections is reconciled to the agent definition; the agent definition is never edited to fit the roster' — NARROW, USER-APPROVED EXCEPTION for this slice only: for code-reviewer / code-reviewer-deep / build-validator the D17 verdict block is a genuinely NEW output contract, so the agent definition is authored first as the authority and the roster's existing required_sections is confirmed against it (no required_sections value actually changes). Do not generalize this exception elsewhere.
No schema_version bump anywhere; 'blocked' is already a member of contract.OUTCOMES and dispatch-record.schema.json's outcome enum; verdict_block already exists in roster.schema.json.
Do NOT touch scripts/cmux/prompts/return-contract.markdown.md — editing it invalidates every judgment role's cached prefix (ADR-009 Am.1) and is not warranted here.
code-reviewer-deep review is REQUIRED on this PR; any scripts/cmux/* edit also routes to the contract-freeze adversarial 3-panel.
acceptance_criteria: contract.mjs exports BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX === 'status: blocked - ' and the closed export-inventory test in test/cmux-contract.test.mjs is extended with it.

return-lint.mjs contains no raw copy of the 'status: blocked - ' literal (it imports the constant); a drift guard pins contract.mjs still declaring it, mirroring the existing WORKER_BLOCKED_STATUSES drift guard.

classify() returns bodyBlockedMarkdown: true only for a completed markdown body starting with the prefix; false for a normal markdown return, a body merely containing the phrase later, and every json return; bodyStatus semantics unchanged (still null for all markdown).
mapOutcome with bodyBlockedMarkdown:true maps to 'blocked'; with bodyBlockedMarkdown:false still maps to 'ok'.

Anti-laundering: a completed markdown return NOT starting with the prefix but carrying verdict 'inconclusive' maps to 'ok', not 'blocked' — a genuine reviewer's legitimate inconclusive must never be misread as gate-killed.

Regression across all six already-pane-enabled markdown roles (plan-reviewer, architecture-lead, backend-lead, frontend-lead, devops-lead, qa-lead): a blocked envelope built via the real writeBlockedReturn output classifies as outcome 'blocked', not a hand-written fixture string.

End-to-end through closeCmd: a dispatch whose return_path holds a gate-composed blocked markdown envelope closes with outcome 'blocked' and exit code 1 (previously 'ok'/0); the existing MF1 positive-control test (a real, non-blocked markdown reviewer return closes ok) stays green.

return-lint.mjs's destinationHoldsFreshNonBlockedReturn is NOT re-keyed (stays byte-identical) — pinned by a regression test proving writeBlockedReturn never clobbers an existing fresh markdown return, blocked-prefixed or not.
The RESIDUAL comment at dispatch.mjs:103-107 is deleted and replaced with a comment describing the new row; grep for RESIDUAL in dispatch.mjs returns nothing.

PANE_ROLES has ten members; test/roster.test.mjs's set-equality against the roster's pane:true roles passes; test/cmux-contract.test.mjs's array deepEqual is updated to the same literal in the same order.

Each of the three agent files authors exactly one heading (level >= 2) whose case-folded text prefix-matches each of its roster required_sections entries — verified by a strengthened EXACTLY-ONE coherence guard (not at-least-one) with a synthetic-shadow non-vacuity control proving the guard can actually detect a shadowing heading.

Each new ## Verdict section contains exactly one fenced json block that validates against return-lint.mjs's VERDICT_SCHEMA — verified by extracting and validating the example block from all three agent files.
node --test test/claude-adapter.test.mjs passes; its PANE_ROLES-driven argv loop now non-vacuously covers three roles that declare disallowedTools frontmatter.
roster.schema.json's verdict_block description no longer says 'Reserved'.

code-reviewer-deep review is required and named in the PR description, along with the #6 shipped-date context for how long the outcome-classifier bug has been live, and the accepted, documentation-only consequence that these three roles lose WebFetch/WebSearch in pane mode (ADR-005 Am.1).
Full suite (node --test) green once before opening the PR.

discovery_context:
SUB-SLICE A. The bug, exactly: scripts/cmux/ladder.mjs:417-424 — `if (completed) { const body = validation.envelope && validation.envelope.body; const bodyStatus = body && typeof body === 'object' && typeof body.status === 'string' ? body.status : null; return { state: 'completed', reason: 'fresh_valid_return', warnings, bodyStatus } }`. A markdown body is a STRING so bodyStatus is always null for it. scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs:102-114 (OUTCOME_MAPPING): the RESIDUAL comment at :103-107 explains this was known-harmless 'while PANE_ROLES is coder-only'; the `completed -> ok` row fires for any completed state regardless of bodyStatus. WORKER_BLOCKED_STATUSES.includes(null) is false, so a gate-killed markdown dispatch is recorded 'ok'. Six roles are already exposed (scripts/cmux/roster.default.json:85-143, all pane:true + kind:markdown, shipped in #6).

The literal to key on: scripts/cmux/return-lint.mjs:333-334, buildBlockedMarkdownBody: `const lines = [`status: blocked - ${sanitizeReasonForMarkdown(reason)}`, '']`. sanitizeReasonForMarkdown (:329-331) collapses every [\r\n]+ to '; ', so the composed first line is always exactly one line beginning with that literal at byte 0 — startsWith on the whole body is exact. Two existing tests already pin this shape: test/return-lint.test.mjs:314 and :393 (`assert.match(result.envelope.body, /^status: blocked - /)`).

Change 1 (scripts/cmux/contract.mjs, after WORKER_BLOCKED_STATUSES at :27): add `export const BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX = 'status: blocked - '` with a comment explaining it's the one shared literal between composer (return-lint.mjs) and recognizer (ladder.mjs), deliberately NOT the verdict enum (a genuine reviewer may legitimately return verdict inconclusive; keying on the enum would misread a real review as gate-killed).

Change 2 (scripts/cmux/return-lint.mjs): extend the contract.mjs import to include BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX; rewrite line 334 to interpolate the imported constant instead of the raw literal. Zero behavior change.

Change 3 (scripts/cmux/ladder.mjs): its import at :13 is `import { validate, SIGNAL_LIMITS, SECTION_HEADING_RE } from './contract.mjs'` — add BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX (ladder -> contract is the existing import direction; never import return-lint.mjs from ladder.mjs, that would be a cycle — return-lint already imports ladder). In the completed branch, after the bodyStatus line, add: `const bodyBlockedMarkdown = typeof body === 'string' && body.startsWith(BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX)` and include it in the returned object. Do not change bodyStatus's derivation. The field is present (and false) on every completed classification including json ones.

Change 4 (scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs): delete the RESIDUAL comment at :103-107; insert a new row BETWEEN the existing worker_blocked row and the completed row: `{ row: 'worker_blocked_markdown', outcome: OUTCOME_WORKER_BLOCKED, when: (c) => c.state === 'completed' && c.bodyBlockedMarkdown === true }` — use === true not truthiness (fail closed if the field is ever absent from an older/partial classification).

Downstream, already correct, do not touch: closeCmd (dispatch.mjs:1195-1272) calls mapOutcome at :1224, applyPostconditionOverride at :1231 (only demotes ok, so blocked passes through unaffected), terminateRecord at :1236, returns exit code 1 for any non-ok outcome at :1265. presentReturn (:1256) is outcome-independent so the doc tab still renders a blocked return. contract.shouldArchive (:245-251) archives on any non-ok outcome — correct new behavior. No schema work needed: contract.OUTCOMES already contains 'blocked' and dispatch-record.schema.json's outcome enum already includes it (landed at fix-1c-00, schema_version already bumped 1->2 then).

THE SECOND SITE — DO NOT COPY THE SAME FIX THERE. scripts/cmux/return-lint.mjs:382-393, destinationHoldsFreshNonBlockedReturn: `const bodyStatus = body && typeof body === 'object' ? body.status : null; return !WORKER_BLOCKED_STATUSES.includes(bodyStatus)`. Same null-reads-as-non-blocked shape, OPPOSITE required behavior: true means 'a legitimate return is already sitting here, don't overwrite it'. For markdown it currently always returns true (always preserves what's on disk). If the same keying were applied here, a body starting with the prefix would return false and the gate would OVERWRITE it — destroying either (a) a previous blocked envelope from this same dispatch (harmless) or (b) a WORKER's own self-authored blocked markdown body and its real verdict json, replaced by the fabricated {"verdict":"inconclusive","findings":[]} stub (return-lint.mjs:99, VERDICT_STUB_OBJECT) — silent evidence loss. Leave this function byte-identical; pin the asymmetry with a regression test (writeBlockedReturn on a destination already holding a fresh valid markdown envelope, blocked-prefixed or not, leaves the file byte-identical and returns return_path) plus a comment at :390 pointing at OUTCOME_MAPPING's worker_blocked_markdown row for the classifier's opposite treatment.

SUB-SLICE B. Roster (scripts/cmux/roster.default.json): three one-token flips, false -> true: build-validator.pane (~:64), code-reviewer.pane (~:72), code-reviewer-deep.pane (~:81). Their return blocks already read `{"kind":"markdown","required_sections":["Verdict"],"verdict_block":true}` and `{"kind":"markdown","required_sections":["Verdict","Must-fix","Notes"],"verdict_block":true}` — no other roster fields change.

scripts/cmux/contract.mjs:44 PANE_ROLES — append the three in roster order: `['coder','plan-reviewer','architecture-lead','backend-lead','frontend-lead','devops-lead','qa-lead','build-validator','code-reviewer','code-reviewer-deep']`. test/cmux-contract.test.mjs deepEquals this ARRAY (order-sensitive) — update to the identical literal. test/roster.test.mjs asserts SET equality against the roster (order-insensitive). ATOMICITY: contract.mjs + roster.default.json + the three agent files + both tests must be ONE commit — split them and the coherence guards go red on the intermediate commit.

Heading structure of the three agent files (read and verified, no existing collision): agents/code-reviewer.md has `## Output — verdict FIRST` (case-folds to 'output — verdict first', does NOT start with 'verdict' — safe, leave alone) plus Reporting bar/Tone/Review Priorities/Escalate When Needed/How You Review/Boundaries — none prefix-match Verdict/Must-fix/Notes. agents/code-reviewer-deep.md similarly has `## Output — verdict FIRST` plus Tone/Deep Review Scope/Security Review Lens/Reporting bar/How You Review/Findings Format/Boundaries — Findings Format does not prefix-match 'must-fix' (the hyphen in 'Must-fix' is load-bearing; a heading 'Must fix' with a space also would not match). agents/build-validator.md has How You Work/Rules only — no collision.

The hazard being guarded (architecture-notes.md 2026-08-03): extractSection (return-lint.mjs:165-173) does `headings.findIndex((h) => h.level >= 2 && h.name.toLowerCase().startsWith(needle))` — FIRST-MATCH-WINS, so a heading like '## Verdict summary' placed before '## Verdict' would shadow it. Author exactly ONE heading per required name; do not put a second Verdict-prefixed heading inside a fenced example — the roster guard is fence-BLIND by design.

Insert, in both code-reviewer.md and code-reviewer-deep.md, immediately AFTER '## Output — verdict FIRST' (before '## How You Review'): a `## Verdict` section with exactly one fenced json block matching `{"verdict": "pass|changes-needed|inconclusive", "findings": [{"severity": "critical|warning|suggestion", "file": "<path>", "line": <int|null>, "summary": "<string>"}]}` (schema at return-lint.mjs:75-96, enums at :69-70), a `## Must-fix` section (bugs/security/data-loss/broken-rollback findings that flip the verdict to changes-needed; per-finding: where, why, fix direction, confidence; 'none' if empty), and a `## Notes` section (Should-fix and Consider findings plus anything the next reviewer should know; 'none' if empty). Keep the existing first-line 'VERDICT:' prose convention intact — it's what agent-tool mode reads. For agents/build-validator.md, insert ONLY a `## Verdict` section after '## How You Work' (before '## Rules'), example `{"verdict": "pass", "findings": []}`, mapping: pass when typecheck/build succeed AND when nothing is configured to run (a no-steps project is a pass per build-validator.md's existing text); changes-needed on any type/compile/build error, one finding per error; inconclusive only when a configured step could not be run at all.

Strengthen test/roster.test.mjs's coherence guard (currently `.some(...)` + assert.ok, roughly :68-80) to assert EXACTLY ONE matching heading (`.filter(...).length === 1`) for every pane+markdown role and required section, with a failure message naming both directions (0 = role doesn't author the section; 2+ = shadowing per extractSection's first-match-wins). Add a non-vacuity control: apply the same local matching predicate to a synthetic ['Verdict summary', 'Verdict'] heading list and assert it returns 2 matches, proving the guard can actually see a shadow. Verified safe against every current role's existing headings (plan-reviewer, architecture-lead, backend/frontend/devops-lead, qa-lead all map required sections to exactly one heading today).

test/claude-adapter.test.mjs: run it, expect green with no assertion edits — its PANE_ROLES-driven argv loop (~:292) becomes non-vacuous for three roles that DO declare disallowedTools frontmatter (the positive control at ~:288-290 already covers this shape). Two comments nearby reference 'this slice' framing and should be corrected as comment-only changes (no logic).

scripts/cmux/roster.schema.json:68 — replace `"verdict_block": { "type": "boolean", "description": "Reserved; prose default false." }` with a description stating true means the Verdict section must carry exactly one fenced json block matching {verdict, findings}, enforced by return-lint.mjs (not by this schema); prose default false. interface_contract: contract.mjs: BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX = 'status: blocked - ' (exact, trailing space included). ladder.classify()'s completed-state return value gains an additive field: bodyBlockedMarkdown: boolean (true iff body is a string starting with BLOCKED_MARKDOWN_PREFIX); bodyStatus keeps its existing null-for-markdown semantics unchanged. dispatch.OUTCOME_MAPPING gains one row 'worker_blocked_markdown' -> outcome 'blocked', evaluated between the existing 'worker_blocked' row and the 'completed' row. contract.PANE_ROLES becomes ['coder','plan-reviewer','architecture-lead','backend-lead','frontend-lead','devops-lead','qa-lead','build-validator','code-reviewer','code-reviewer-deep']. No other task in this batch shares these shapes; qa-3b-01 (qa-gate.md doctrine) references outcome 'blocked' conceptually but does not consume this interface directly.
